officialSection:
Official Information

  • Grab's driver requirements: Malaysian aged 21 to 69 with a blue NRIC, a Malaysian Competent Driving Licence, an E-Hailing PSV Licence, a vehicle not older than 15 years, E-Hailing Vehicle Insurance, and a personal bank account matching the NRIC. Grab Malaysia, driver page
  • Grab's reimbursements (limited time, T&Cs apply): PSV licence RM20, medical check-up RM50 to RM80, EVP RM110, Puspakom RM70; PSV training cost varies by city. Grab Malaysia, driver page
  • EVP: Grab processes eligible EVP applications in the APAD system, taking about 5 working days. The vehicle must be no older than 15 years, with a civilian-ID owner who is a Malaysian citizen or permanent resident, and JPJ vehicle code AB or AD (pick-up trucks are excluded). Grab Malaysia, EVP process
  • APAD rules: E-hailing drivers must be Malaysian citizens, registered with a licensed e-hailing operator, hold a valid JPJ PSV vocational licence, and drive a vehicle with a valid eVP issued by APAD; driving without these may be penalised under the Land Public Transport Act 2010. APAD Knowledge Base
  • Where permits are issued: APAD handles e-hailing vehicle permits through its iSPKP commercial vehicle licensing system. APAD

discrepancies.suggestedReplacement: • Puspakom inspection where required (Grab currently reimburses RM70 for it)

discrepancies.existing: • E-hailing PSV licence (Grab currently subsidises the PSV training, licence, and medical check-up)
discrepancies.official: Grab reimburses PSV training (varies by city), PSV licence RM20, medical RM50-RM80, EVP RM110, Puspakom RM70, 'Limited Time Only', T&Cs apply.
discrepancies.suggestedReplacement: (Grab currently reimburses PSV-related costs for a limited time; terms apply)

discrepancies.existing: • A car not older than 15 years, registered in your own name
discrepancies.official: Grab lists 'a vehicle that's not older than 15 years' plus a vehicle ownership certificate; the EVP page requires the owner to be a Malaysian citizen/PR with civilian ID (not company/police/military). 'Own name' is not stated verbatim.
discrepancies.suggestedReplacement: • A car not older than 15 years, with ownership documents (the owner must be a Malaysian citizen or permanent resident with a civilian ID)

discrepancies.existing: Step 2: Upload documents — licence, NRIC, vehicle registration with valid roadtax, insurance.
discrepancies.official: Grab's steps: register in app, get PSV licence with Grab's help, arrange E-Hailing Vehicle Insurance, submit documents, verification, start earning. E-Hailing Vehicle Insurance is a stated requirement (article says only 'insurance'); also 'not previously banned or terminated as a Grab Driver-Partner'.
discrepancies.suggestedReplacement: Optional: add 'E-Hailing Vehicle Insurance' wording and the not-previously-banned condition. Age 21-69, 15-year limit, EVP, bank account all match the article.

discrepancies.existing: Since October 2019, e-hailing drivers in Malaysia must hold a PSV (Public Service Vehicle) licence.
discrepancies.official: APAD confirms PSV licence is required; the October 2019 start date was not on any official page fetched (only seen in a non-official news search result). Unverified date.
discrepancies.suggestedReplacement: E-hailing drivers in Malaysia must hold a PSV (Public Service Vehicle) licence from JPJ.
